questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Define the following terms as used in Crystallography:

(i) Crystal face: (2 marks)

(ii) Crystal form: (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Crystal face** is a flat, smooth natural surface that bounds a crystal; it is the outside expression of the regular internal arrangement of the atoms.

**(ii) Crystal form** is a set of crystal faces that are all alike in size, shape and relation to the crystallographic axes, because they are related by the symmetry of the crystal (e.g. the six square faces of a cube make one form).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Differentiate between cleavage and fracture of a mineral.

(2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Cleavage** is the tendency of a mineral to break along smooth, flat, parallel planes of weakness in its atomic structure (e.g. mica, calcite, halite).

**Fracture** is the way a mineral breaks in directions that are *not* planes of weakness, giving irregular or curved surfaces (e.g. the conchoidal, shell-like fracture of quartz).

So cleavage gives regular, flat, repeatable surfaces, while fracture gives irregular surfaces.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Distinguish between marine transgression and regression.

(2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Marine transgression** is the advance (spread) of the sea over the land, caused by a rise in sea level or a sinking of the land; the shoreline moves inland and finer, deeper-water sediments are deposited over coarser, shallow-water ones.

**Marine regression** is the retreat of the sea from the land, caused by a fall in sea level or an uplift of the land; the shoreline moves seaward and coarser, shallow-water sediments are deposited over finer ones, leaving land exposed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) State TWO effects of earthquakes.

(2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any two of the following:

1. Collapse of buildings, bridges and roads, causing loss of life and injuries.
2. Landslides and rock falls, and cracks (fissures) opening in the ground.
3. Tsunamis when the epicentre is under the sea.
4. Fires and floods from broken gas pipes, electric cables and dams.
5. Liquefaction of loose, wet soil.
